newsitem.title: UK: S&P rates AON unit's capital securities.
newsitem.headline: S&P rates AON unit's capital securities.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Tuesday it assigned its AA minus rating to Aon Capital A's $700 million Rule 144A capital securities due 2027 and has placed it on CreditWatch with negative implications.
S&P said in a statement the ratings of Aon Corp and related entities remain on CreditWatch with negative implications. Approximately $633 million of total Aon debt is outstanding.
"The rating on Aon Capital A is based on the full and unconditional guarantee of Aon Corp," the agency said.
It said the capital securities were part of the financing of Aon's pending acquisition of Alexander & Alexander Services Inc. (A&A) in a transaction valued at approximately $1.23 billion.
Aon, which owns Aon Group, the second-largest insurance broker in the world by 1995 gross revenues, has agreed to acquire A&A, the fourth-largest insurance broker, S&P said.

The transaction involves paying $790 million of cash to A&A common stock holders, $317.5 million to purchase A&A's series B preferred shares held by American International Group, Inc., and assuming A&A's series A preferred shares.
"This acquisition is consistent with Aon's strategy as a consolidator in the insurance brokerage industry, although the size of the proposed transaction exceeds S&P's expectations," the agency said.
While S&P expects that Aon will produce cost savings from A&A over the long-term, Standard & Poor's believes Aon will be challenged to improve A&A's weaker business profile.

In addition, S&P said Aon's ultimate financing for the acquisition will increase financial leverage significantly above its current target range, and resulting coverages may fall below historically excellent levels.
Increased fixed-charge needs may also require greater dependence on Combined to upstream dividends, it said.
